chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah said:

I found in the Sheet of Inheritance shares: 'A man died and left behind a daughter and two parents. I found for the daughter three shares, and for the two parents, for each one of them, one share. The wealth is divided into five parts. Whatever portion amounts to three parts is for the daughter, and whatever portion amounts to two parts is for the two parents.'
ai.seo_question: How is an estate divided when a person leaves a daughter and both parents?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahifat al-Fara'id highlights the foundational juristic reasoning (ijtihad) of the Imams, specifically illustrating how the daughter's share is fixed at one-half (three-fifths in this specific calculation context relative to the total pool) while parents receive the residual or fixed portions. It serves as a key example of the Shia methodology where the Quranic verse 4:11 is interpreted to grant the daughter a half-share when she is the sole child, and the parents receive one-sixth each, though this specific text reflects a particular scholarly calculation of dividing the estate into five parts to accommodate these shares. This case is significant for understanding the interplay between the 'Asabah' (residuary heirs) and fixed-share heirs in Shia inheritance law.
